record.notes: The document is dated December 2025 on its cover. By 1 April 2026 Cabinet had approved the strategy and USD 250 million for a national AI computing centre. President John Dramani Mahama launched the strategy in Accra on Friday 24 April 2026, when USD 20 million was also announced for its short- and medium-term implementation. At the launch the Minister for Communication said the ministry was working on an Emerging Technologies Bill to provide the legal framework for AI and related technologies. The strategy rests on about 40 expert interviews and public-sector consultation workshops held from March to October 2022, and recommends reducing the implementation timeline from ten to five years with periodic reviews.
record.scope_note: Mainly a strategy for AI education, skills, infrastructure, data, research and adoption; included as Ghana's national AI strategy, which analyses AI risks and proposes a Responsible AI Authority, incident reporting, safe-AI guidance for developers and tools to audit and certify AI systems.

verification.note: Recheck of 18 Oct 2026. Stored: the strategy PDF from moc.gov.gh (84 pages; stored 11 Oct 2026 and unchanged on 18 Oct 2026), the ministry's release of 24 April 2026 on the launch (moc.gov.gh), the Information Services Department's report of 1 April 2026 on Cabinet's approval (isd.gov.gh), and the Ghana News Agency report of the launch (a state news agency, not an official source; new snapshot of 18 Oct 2026 that differs from the earlier one only in page furniture). The PDF confirms the title, the issuing ministry, the December 2025 date, the eight pillars, the risk analysis, the Responsible AI Authority and National AI Office proposals and the governance actions in the summary. The ministry's release confirms the launch by the President in Accra on 24 April 2026; the ISD report confirms Cabinet's approval of the strategy and of USD 250 million for an AI computing centre. The USD 20 million for implementation and the Emerging Technologies Bill rest on the news agency's report; no text of an Emerging Technologies Bill was found. The '2023/03' in the PDF's path is the site's upload folder, not the document's date.

judgment.status_reasoning: A non-binding national strategy for 2025-2035 published by the ministry (cover dated December 2025), approved by Cabinet by 1 April 2026 (ISD) and launched by the President in Accra on 24 April 2026 (ministry release). Nothing stored shows it withdrawn or replaced; it is within its period. Published (non-binding, current).
judgment.scope_reasoning: In scope as Ghana's national AI strategy with a risk analysis and governance proposals (Responsible AI Authority, incident reporting, safe-AI guidance, audit and certification tools, insurance for high-risk outputs). Its main content is adoption, skills and infrastructure, so a scope_note is added under the rule for strategies with some safety content.
judgment.date_reasoning: The cover gives 'DECEMBER 2025' and no day, so date_published stays 2025-12. Cabinet's approval (by 1 April 2026; the report does not give the day of the Cabinet meeting) and the launch on 24 April 2026 are later events and stay in notes.
judgment.topics_reasoning: incident reporting (National AI Office mandate for incident reporting), accountability & liability (insurance for high-risk AI outputs, accountability and legal clarity), evaluation & testing (auditing and certifying AI systems; oversight of AI system qualification), public-sector use (Pillar 8), research priorities (Pillar 7, applied research).
